advances: An actual ordinary-depth separator on a fixed selected whole-plane cover; the cap parameters may move but energy-buffer contact is not modeled.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Split the cap mass difference into the fixed-body cap motion and the body change measured in the moving cap. The fixed-body part follows from the fiberwise slicing formula (4)–(5) of 6b80e85ff6937910 with density velocity zero. For the second part integrate along the old radial rays. At an old regular boundary point, change the radial shell variable to outward normal distance $t\tau$ to first order; the Jacobian is the old surface measure as in the defining-field variation lemma. The signed shell range is from $0$ to $r$. Away from the cap plane the indicator is eventually constant. A proper intersection with the old boundary has zero surface area, since its trace in the plane is the relative boundary of the full section. At an inside supporting facet the outer body normal is $-v_j$, so the limiting shell indicator is $\mathbf1_{\{\tau\le\ell_j\}}$; at an outside supporting facet it is $\mathbf1_{\{\tau\ge-\ell_j\}}$. Uniform shell bounds and dominated convergence apply, since equality in the limiting indicator is a single shell-coordinate value. Add the fixed-body contributions: $\min(0,\ell_j)+\int_0^r\mathbf1_{\{\tau\le\ell_j\}}\,d\tau=\min(r,\ell_j)$ and $\max(0,\ell_j)+\int_0^r\mathbf1_{\{\tau\ge-\ell_j\}}\,d\tau=\max(r+\ell_j,0)$. The same proof counts endpoints for $d=1$. These formulas show that the true derivative is bounded above by $\sup_{g\in G_j}g$, since any prescribed inside convex average dominates the minimum and an outside subdensity realizes the maximum. Finite moments of weak-star compact subdensities make the gradient sets compact convex.

All assigned margins and normal balances persist along the affine cap paths, so the old full-plane cover persists. In common erosion every $g_j$ is strictly negative, bounded away from zero uniformly in the allocations for each $j$: the proper own anchor cut has a relatively open boundary patch of positive surface area strictly inside, and all other body coefficients are nonnegative. The cone $\sum_j\mathbb R_+G_j+D^\circ$ is closed, since evaluation at this erosion direction bounds the total nonnegative coefficients of any convergent sequence in the cone. Compactness then gives limits of the cap parts and hence of the polar parts. If $L_0$ were outside, separation would give a direction in $D$ on which $L_0>0$ and every cap form is nonpositive. Adding a sufficiently small amount of erosion preserves $L_0>0$ and gives strict negativity for every critical cap. Along the actual defining-field variation with affine cap motion the mass increases, every critical budget falls below $Q$, and strict slack remains. The persistent cover then implies normalized depth below $\beta$, a contradiction.

For signed joint homothety use $r=u\cdot x$ on the normal bundle and $\delta v_j=0,\ \delta a_j=a_j,\ \delta b_j=b_j$. The weighted margin derivatives vanish at all active assigned bases, so both signs belong to $D$ and the polar term vanishes there. The actual exact scaling of the body and cap thresholds gives derivatives $dM$ and $dQ$. These are also the evaluations of every corresponding allocated form: on the plane $\ell_j=-v_j\cdot x$, so $r=\ell_j$ on inside facets and $r=-\ell_j$ on outside facets. The true and allocated derivatives therefore agree there and on all other parts. Consequently $dM=dQ\sum_j\lambda_j$, as claimed.
statement:
Let a finite positive actual fiber family as in the defining-field variation lemma locally minimize maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth among such families in the fiber Hausdorff topology, with raw maximum $Q=\beta M>0$. Fix a finite exact critical circuit cover of all deepest bases and fixed strictly cheaper covers elsewhere. Each critical cap $H_j=\{a_j\cdot z+v_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$ has mass $Q$, unit continuous normal and a proper own anchor through an interior deepest mark. In each group fix positive weights $\rho_j$ with $\sum_j\rho_j v_j=0$ and assign bases on which the weighted constant margin is nonnegative. On a finite list of defining-field tests from the defining-field variation lemma allow free signed affine terms and nonnegative coefficients of convex potential terms. Append cap velocities preserving weighted normal balance and having nonnegative derivative of every active assigned margin. Include common erosion $r=-1$ and signed joint continuous homothety in the list. Denote this velocity cone by $D$, and write $\ell_j=\delta a_j\cdot z+\delta v_j\cdot x-\delta b_j$ for each cap's margin change.

The actual right cap derivative has the body speed $r$ on strict captured boundary, zero on strict excluded boundary, the ordinary $\ell_j$ integral on proper sections, and the branches $\min(r,\ell_j)$ on inside supporting facets and $\max(r+\ell_j,0)$ on outside supporting facets, integrated with fiber surface area. Fix any Borel inside body subdensities $0\le\alpha_j\le1$. Let $G_j$ be the compact convex set of linear forms $g_j=\int\alpha_j r\,d\eta+\int\ell_j\,d\zeta_j$, where $\alpha_j$ is the strict boundary indicator off coincidences, the section measure $\zeta_j$ has full proper section area, and its facet subdensity $\sigma_j$ is $1-\alpha_j$ on inside facets and $\alpha_j\in[0,1]$ on outside facets. There exist $g_j\in G_j$ and $\lambda_j\ge0$ such that
$$
L_0=\sum_j\lambda_j g_j+L,\qquad L_0=\int r\,d\eta,\qquad L\in D^\circ,\qquad \sum_j\lambda_j=1/\beta,
$$
where $D^\circ$ consists of forms nonpositive on $D$. The cap derivative formula applies also to any body path with uniform $O(t)$ radial displacement and the indicated regular radial derivative.
title: Consistent supporting-facet gradients give normalized moving-cap separation
